newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian PM to look at Fahey share details.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian PM to look at Fahey share details.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Thursday he would investigate reports that Finance Minister John Fahey had misled the parliament about his shareholding in a private company.
"All I can say is I will investigate that," Howard told Sydney radio 2UE. "There may be a completely innocent explanation of that."

Howard was unaware of a report in the Australian Financial Review newspaper that Fahey had declared a 50 percent interest in Tunboa Pty Ltd to the New South Wales state parliament in each of the 10 years up to 1995.
But Fahey told both Howard and parliament on Wednesday that he sold his Tunboa holding in 1986, saying the buyer had failed to register the transfer.
"What you put to me is something new to me," Howard said in the radio interview.

The discrepancy is the latest incident in a week-long controversy over breaches of Howard's ministerial guidelines, under which government members are required to divest any investments in which may conflict with their portfolio area.
The controversy has forced two government members to resign and the opposition is targeting another three.
Howard said he had "done his block" behind closed doors over the ministerial share row.

"I certainly did. I think people have been careless," he said. "Nobody's been dishonest, nobody's made a cent out of any of this, but in a couple of cases rules have been laid down and people haven't bothered to read the rules or give sufficient attention to them.
"They've paid a price for that," he said.
A spokesman for Fahey earlier told Reuters the discrepancy was "an oversight" on the minister's part.
